translations.text: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the churches of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing greatly, and the love of each one of you for one another is increasing,
so that we ourselves boast of you in the churches of God, for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are enduring,
as a sign of the righteous judgment of God, so that you may be made worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering.
If indeed it is just with God that affliction should come upon those who afflict you,
and that you who are afflicted should have rest with us, on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ's revelation from heaven with the angels of his power,
in flaming fire, to repay vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who have not obeyed the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ,
on whom judgment will be brought, eternal torment, away from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his might,
when he comes to be glorified among his saints and to be marveled at among all who believe, because our testimony to you was believed, on that day,
for which we pray for you, that our God may make you worthy of the calling and fill you with every goodness of kindness, and with the work of faith, and with power,
so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified among you, and you through him, by the grace of our God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.
This I say to you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him:
that you not be quickly shaken in your mind, and not be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter, as if from us, as though the day of the Lord had already come.
Let no one deceive you in any way, for that day will not come until the apostasy comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of perdition,
the adversary, who exalts himself above everything that is called god or an object of worship, so that he even sits in the temple of God and displays himself as God.
Do you not remember that while I was still with you I told you this?
And now you know what you have been taught [?]: that he is to be revealed in his own time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who now holds it back will do so until he is taken far out of the way,
and then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord will destroy with the breath of his mouth and bring to nothing by the appearance of his coming,
the one whose coming is by the working of the devil, with all power and with signs of falsehood,
and with every deception of lies among those who are perishing, because they did not accept the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
And for this reason God will send them a deluding influence, so that they will believe the lie,
so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in falsehood.
But we ought always to give thanks for you, beloved brothers, by the Lord, because God chose you as firstfruits for life, through sanctification by the Spirit and faith in the truth,
to which he also called you through our gospel, so that you might obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So from now on, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to this teaching that you have learned, whether by word or by this letter of ours.
And may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.
From now on, brothers, pray for us, that the word of God may spread and be glorified, just as it was among you,
and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked people, for not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful, and he will make you firm and guard you from evil.
I trust in the Lord concerning you, that you are doing and will keep doing what we commanded you.
And may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and the patience of Christ.
I command you, brothers, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from every brother who lives in a disorderly way and not according to the teaching that he learned from us.
You yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, for we did nothing improper among you.
We did not eat anyone's bread for nothing. Instead we worked night and day with labor and toil, so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
It was not that I do not have the right, but that we might give ourselves to you as an example, so that you would imitate us.
And when I was with you, we gave you this command: if anyone does not want to work, he should not eat either.
For I hear about some who conduct themselves among you in a disorderly way: they do no work, but go around as busybodies.
We command and urge such people through the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers, do not grow weary of doing good.
If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of him and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.
Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
Now may the God of peace himself give you peace always and in every way. The Lord be with you all!
The greeting in my own hand, which is the sign in every letter. This is how I write:
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
